title: Septic Shock: Recognition and Initial Management
mission: Recognize pediatric septic shock and walk the initial-management sequence.
checkpoints: Require age over 28 days and at most 18 years, a temperature abnormality or concern for infection, and the shock findings in the standard's tables.
Stop for trauma, age 0 through 28 days, and pregnancy.
Follow the first-hour actions in the order the algorithm prints them.
mayPropose: Unsigned fluid, culture, antibiotic, and support orders quoted in algorithm order.
cardSummary: TCH septic shock standard may apply. Confirm age and the shock findings in the tables.

population.inclusion: All pediatric patients greater than 28 days old with a temperature abnormality and/or concern for infection AND who meet one of the following criteria:; Three or more of the identified signs and symptoms of shock (Table 3) and/or abnormal vital signs (Table 2); High risk patient (Table 1) AND two or more of the identified signs and symptoms of shock (Table 3) and/or abnormal vital signs (Table 2); Hypotension (refer to Table 2) Table 1. High Risk Conditions Malignancy Sickle Cell Disease and other patients with asplenia Bone marrow transplant Central or indwelling line/catheter Solid organ transplant Severe mental retardation/cerebral palsy Immunodeficiency, immunocompromised or immunosuppression Urogenital abnormalities (i.e. spina bifida) Table 2.
population.exclusion: Trauma; Neonates (0-28 days old); Pregnancy; Age > 18 years
